body: FLAGS: GAAP losses every year until 2020; repeated equity raises; in 2020 alone $2 bn (Feb), $5 bn at-the-market (Sep) and $5 bn at-the-market (Dec) = $12 bn; extreme short interest; P/E >100 at the 2021 peak. CONTEXT: by mid-2019 the Model 3 ramp (~5k/week), a surprise Q3-2019 profit and the Shanghai factory built in ~10 months showed the survival risk was ending. The 2020 share sales were made after a ~650% rally at a ~$500 bn valuation, so each $5 bn was only ~1% dilution: cheap capital that fully funded new factories (Giga Texas) and removed bankruptcy risk. Dilution at a high price, for growth capex, is a gift to existing holders; dilution at a low price to survive is a transfer from them. Stock: ~$11.8 split-adjusted (Jun 2019) -> ~$414 (Nov 2021), ~35x. WHERE THE FLAG CAME TRUE: the price was mostly rerating; it fell -73% to ~$101 (Jan 2023) when auto margins fell. LESSON: measure dilution as % of shares and ask the price and purpose; separate 'will it survive?' from 'is it worth this price?'.

data.context: survival risk resolved; raises at peak valuation ~1% each; funded capex
data.lesson: dilution: price x purpose x % of shares
data.verdict: survival flag false; valuation flag real

title: False alarm (on survival), real (on valuation): Tesla's losses and $12 bn of share sales
